sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture and Canning of Retort River Snail Noodles (Luosifen)

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Law heritage with Luxembourg-specific commercial and company law codifications)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaties, including BLEU-China BIT
Luxembourg-United States Double Taxation Convention (signed 1996, as amended)
EU free trade agreements applicable through Luxembourg's EU membership, such as EU-Japan EPA, EU-Singapore FTA, and EU-Vietnam FTA

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law); Law of 27 June 2019 implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; Grand-Ducal Regulations issued under the AML/CFT framework; CSSF Circulars 18/698 and 20/744; Luxembourg Criminal Code provisions on corruption and terrorist financing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft Articles of Association (Acte constitutif / Statuts)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Luxembourg notarial deed (acte authentique); no apostille required because executed before a Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport for each shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of each shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for non-EU public documents; notarized certified copy for EU/EEA documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or corporate registry extract for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry in shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for signatory states; consular legalization through the Luxembourg embassy/consulate for non-signatory states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (if incorporation is signed through a local or appointed agent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization when executed abroad; otherwise notarized before a Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / proof of capital payment undertaking
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Credit institution at which the initial share capital is blocked
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private instrument; signature notarization may be required by the Luxembourg notary; apostille is not customary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, authorized representatives, and UBOs against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and Luxembourg national asset-freezing orders. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs) under the Luxembourg AML Law and CSSF Circulars. Suspicious transactions must be reported to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier - CRF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) accessible through MyGuichet.lu and the LBR portal (lbr.lu); online name reservation via MyGuichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin-alphabet characters; non-Latin script names must be romanized/transliterated. The legal form suffix must be the French form 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the accepted abbreviations 'SARL' / 's.à r.l.'. English designations such as 'Ltd.' or 'LLC' are not accepted for a Luxembourg SARL.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 days of a name-refusal notice, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request through MyGuichet.lu to the Luxembourg Business Registers, attaching revised name options and legal arguments. If the refusal is upheld, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Tribunal administratif (Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal) within three months of notification, in accordance with the amended law of 1 December 2015 on administrative procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable as the sole statutory registered office for a SARL engaged in food manufacturing. The registered office must be a real physical address in Luxembourg where legal documents can be served and the company's books and records may be inspected. A virtual-office service may only supplement, not replace, the physical substance requirement for an active industrial licence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — approximately 70% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Luxembourg Food Safety Administration (ALVA) within the first 12 months after obtaining the establishment licence, due to mandatory food hygiene and production-safety supervision.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation and drafting of Articles of Association (SARL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official notarial tariff based on subscribed capital; customary market range EUR 1,500–3,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration and publication costs, including Mémorial / RESA electronic gazette publication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and Luxembourg Official Journal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS filing tariff and official gazette publication fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE (Register of Beneficial Owners) electronic filing
Apostille / consular legalization fees for foreign corporate documents (passport copies, certificates of good standing, powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-country competent authorities and Luxembourg consular posts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille fee (typically EUR 20–80) plus translation and notarization disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Establishment permit application fee for food manufacturing licence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of the Economy and ALVA (Luxembourg Food Safety Administration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative fee for establishment licence and health-permit processing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC due diligence and UBO verification professional fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate service provider or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for pre-incorporation AML/CFT screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign documents into French, German, or Luxembourgish
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-page or per-word sworn translator tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address and physical correspondence services (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market annual fee; does not substitute the requireed physical manufacturing establishment

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as revised; SARL governed by Articles 710-1 to 710-26.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) operating the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) embodying the articles of association (statuts), filed electronically with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of EUR 12,000 (Article 710-1). Capital must be fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation; cash contributions are deposited into a blocked notary or escrow bank account before the notarial deed is signed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that each subscriber named in the share register hereby subscribes and takes up the shares set opposite their name with full payment in accordance with the notarial deed; that the registered office at Luxembourg is adopted as the statutory seat; that the appointed managers, acting severally or jointly, are authorized to open bank accounts, execute the RCS filing and represent the company for permits; that the corporate seal is approved; and that the managers are authorized to file all tax, social security, and food-establishment declarations necessary to commence business in conformity with the Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name availability check and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform an online name availability search on the LBR portal and reserve the proposed SARL name. The reservation is normally made by the notary to ensure compliance with Luxembourg naming rules and to avoid identical or confusingly similar registrations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a request for re-examination with LBR or amend the name to a distinguishable form and reserve again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of articles and notarial deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary in the district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary to draft the French-language articles of association. The deed must be signed before the notary by each shareholder or legal representative; the notary verifies capacity, AML/KYC documentation and the validity of the corporate purpose for food manufacturing.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each shareholder and manager
Corporate documents and power of attorney if shareholder is a legal entity
For in-kind contributions: valuation report of a réviseur d'entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises questions, supplement missing KYC or amend the articles; the notary will reschedule execution once the dossier is regularized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked account and payment of capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or notary's segregated escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked bank account in the name of the SARL in formation. Deposit the full subscribed capital in cash or, for in-kind contributions, attach the statutory valuation report. Obtain a bank certificate confirming the deposit for attachment to the notarial deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank asks for additional AML documentation, provide prompt clarification; if a new bank refuses, transfer the blocked deposit to another authorized bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS (Luxembourg Business Registers) – online filing by notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the notarial deed, bank certificate, appointment consents, and managers' criminal records electronically. Upon verification, the RCS issues a certificate of registration and publication is made in the electronic compendium of companies and associations (RESA).
required_dossiers: Certificate of criminal record for each manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, the notary files a corrective submission or an additional explanatory document within the requested time; rejection may be cured by re-filing a rectified deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, social security and statistical registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Statec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SARL for corporate income tax with ACD, obtain a VAT number from AEDT if taxable supplies exceed the threshold or if immediate VAT filing is elected, register as an employer with CCSS, and complete the business register statement with Statec.
required_dossiers: Lease or proof of business premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, contact the relevant administration to obtain an acknowledgement and rectification; any missing extract can be replaced by the RCS certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment permit and food establishment approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie; Administration Vétérinaire et Alimentaire (ALVA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the business establishment application (auto-rémission d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011 with the Ministry of Economy. In parallel, register the instant noodle manufacturing plant as a food business operator with ALVA and obtain any health approval required for the production, storage and distribution of rice noodles.
required_dossiers: Professional competence evidence or delegated qualified manager
Environmental operational documents for the classified installation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the business permit or food approval is queried, submit an explanatory memorandum to the competent ministry or ALVA within the notification period; if refused, appeal through the administrative review procedure of the Grand-Ducal regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction Générale de la Compétitivité, de la Consommation et de la Propriété Intellectuelle; Administration Vétérinaire et Alimentaire (ALVA) for food safety; Administration de l'Environnement for classified establishments.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) and Agrément sanitaire ALVA (food establishment health approval).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), under the Ministry of Environment, Climate and Biodiversity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 2 classified establishment under the amended Law of 10 June 1999 relating to classified establishments; an environmental impact assessment is required if the production capacity reaches Annex A thresholds, otherwise an environmental registration screening or simplified EIA is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with municipal sewer standards: COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, total suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L, pH 6.5–9, oil and grease ≤ 15 mg/L; VOC and odor emissions must meet the EU Industrial Emissions Directive best available techniques; solid waste and food-processing residues must be segregated and collected by an approved waste operator under Luxembourg waste management law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS), structural load inspection by an approved technical control office (bureau de contrôle technique), and workplace compliance clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) for direct taxes and VAT; Luxembourg Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, AEDT) for VAT registration; single citizen/business portal: MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing or registering in Luxembourg must first obtain a Luxembourg business identification number (matricule d'identification) via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) eRegistration platform or through MyGuichet.lu. For VAT purposes, the foreign taxable person must apply for a Luxembourg VAT number (numéro de TVA) by submitting Form 104 or the applicable eForm to the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu, appointing a VAT representative where required for non-EU established persons. The application must state the intended effective date of taxable activity, expected turnover, and the nature of supplies. Upon approval, the AEDT issues the VAT identification number. Foreign entities established in another EU Member State may instead register under the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) regime for distance sales or non-established business-to-consumer services; a fixed establishment or direct taxable B2B supplies may require a local Luxembourg VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The Luxembourg SARL is subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune), with no check-the-box transparency election available. Statutory elections include: (i) group taxation/fiscal unity for corporate income tax and municipal business tax where a resident parent holds at least 95% of a resident subsidiary for at least one full tax year; (ii) VAT group registration (assujetti unique) for vertically integrated or economically linked Luxembourg entities; (iii) optional 50% net wealth tax deduction for entities owned by tax transparent persons; and (iv) hybrid mismatch election options limited to aligning treatment under ATAD / DAC6 for EU cross-border structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual taxable turnover for the small business exemption; mandatory VAT registration is required for any taxable person making taxable supplies in Luxembourg that exceed this threshold or for non-established foreign suppliers providing distance sales to Luxembourg consumers exceeding EUR 10,000 per calendar year, and for businesses engaged in supplies subject to reverse charge or with a Luxembourg fixed establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory in Luxembourg exclusively for business-to-government (B2G) transactions, requiring structured e-invoices in PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format transmitted through the PEPPOL network; submission is via the MyGuichet.lu portal or direct access points. For business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-consumer (B2C) invoices, there is no real-time fiscal clearance requirement, no mandatory continuous transaction controls (CTCs), and no digital stamping regime. Luxembourg does not currently operate an API-based real-time transaction reporting system like those in Italy or France; however, taxpayers must retain full audit trails and issue invoices electronically or on paper in compliance with EU VAT Directive invoicing rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (i) the supply of goods dispatched or transported to a destination outside the European Union by a Luxembourg taxable person or on its behalf; (ii) supplies of goods covered by the customs warehousing or free-zone procedures; and (iii) supplies of services directly connected with the export or to recipients established outside the EU, provided the recipient is a taxable person or the service falls under specific territoriality rules. For instant rice noodle manufacturing, typical export zero-rating is available when the seller retains valid export proof showing the goods physically left EU territory and entered a third country; the goods must be exported within 3 months of supply, and the manufacturer must hold appropriate documentation to evidence both the export and the receipt of payment from the foreign buyer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ENS/SAD) - Declaration of Export (Déclaration d'exportation) with assigned MRN (Movement Reference Number)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical dispatch from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT payment evidence from the foreign buyer proving repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax authorities may deny zero-rating if the exporter fails to provide conclusive proof of physical export within the statutory period or lacks valid payment evidence. In audit, the AEDT may retrospectively assess VAT at the standard 17% rate on invoiced amounts, plus late-payment interest (intérêts de retard) and penalties for tax fraud or negligence. For fraudulent export zero-rating claims (e.g., fictitious exports, forged shipping documents, or unrepatriated proceeds), penalties may reach up to 100% of the tax evaded, and criminal prosecution is possible under Luxembourg tax law. The statute of limitations for assessments is generally 5 years, extended to 10 years for fraud, and joint liability may be imposed on directors and VAT representatives.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking conduct and prudential AML supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg, as a euro-area member state, maintains full current and capital account convertibility under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the EU Capital Movement Directive (Dir. 88/361/EEC). No exchange-control approval, conversion restriction, or prior authorization is required for ordinary business transactions, capital contributions, dividends, or profit repatriation. The practical remittance hurdles are corporate-law based: certified annual accounts, a timely shareholder meeting, statutory auditor certification where required, and compliance with dividend distribution tests under Luxembourg company law; non-resident shareholders may face Luxembourg withholding tax of 15% on dividends unless reduced by an applicable double tax treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no holding-period restriction on export receipts. Export invoices may be denominated in EUR or any freely convertible currency, and receivables may be retained in foreign currency accounts; only standard accounting, controllers, and VAT invoice requirements apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility for auxiliary cross-border cash movements but Low for primary corporate treasury. EEA-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) passporting into Luxembourg under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) may legally hold transactional funds and issue IBANs; however, Tier-1 Luxembourg lenders generally will not extend credit, issue commercial documentary LCs, or provide committed FX lines at an EMI. CSSF-regulated payment institutions and EMIs are also subject to client-money safeguarding rules and may impose balance or turnover thresholds less suited to a manufacturing company's high-value trade payments. Legal and operational risks include unavailability of MT103 correspondent messaging, potentially narrower UBO/KYC evidence requirements, and lack of insolvency protection under a banking license.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not an absolute statutory mandate under Luxembourg AML/CDD rules. Remote onboarding is permitted where the bank uses CSSF-accepted video-identification or qualified electronic signature processes, subject to a risk-based approach. In practice, tier-1 banks often request at least one physical or videoconference interview of the directors and the 25%+ beneficial owner before opening a commercial account for a newly incorporated SARL with non-resident shareholders; certified copies of constitutional documents and notarized proof of identity may substitute for travel. The higher the onboarding risk score, the more likely a physical or live interview and enhanced due diligence will be required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SARL with non-resident individual shareholders and no audited financial history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original/notarized articles of association; valid passport and proof of residential address of each director and UBO; Luxembourg Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) extracts; pre-filing capital deposit confirmation; comprehensive business plan covering instant rice-noodle manufacturing; expected transaction volumes; supplier/customer lists; third-party due diligence report and sanctions screening results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or director resident in a non-EEA or higher-risk jurisdiction exposing sanctions/BVI concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions and adverse-media screening results; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, including bank reference letters, tax returns, and audited shareholder financial statements; explanations of family/source of capital; notarized UBO declaration; legal opinion on non-sanctioned status; evidence of direct beneficial ownership chain through RBE filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Manufacturing/export cash-flow pattern showing high-value or structurally rapid inbound-outbound flows possibly perceived as trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders/sales contracts with actual commercial terms; customs declarations/CMR waybills; EU/co-manufacturing certification for food products; invoices and packing lists; warehouse receipts; freight insurance; expected margin analysis; bank statements supporting correlation between trade cycles and requested outgoing payments; manager attestation on business purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Demand for multiple currencies with no demonstrated hedging policy or treasury capability.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury and FX risk policy; periodic cash-flow forecast in EUR and trade currencies; confirmation of corporate authorizations and signature mandates; evidence of negotiated trade terms explaining currency exposure; existing letters of intent from wholesale distributors in export markets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a high-risk bank as referrer or refusal by another EU bank due to incomplete documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete re-KYC in line with CSSF AML/CFT circulars; explicit remediation memo identifying reasons for earlier refusal; refreshed RBE and sanctions screening; independent AML audit or compliance consultant opinion; board resolution ratifying the account mandate; confirmation that all transactions are supported by standard ISIC 1079 commercial contracts and traceable inventory.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant methodology: inward remittance from the ultimate shareholder or financing entity to the SARL's dedicated capital escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution using SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer where both accounts are within SEPA. The message must specify the beneficiary SARL with complete IBAN/BIC, the payment reference 'Souscription au capital social' or 'Share capital contribution', and an ISO 20022 external purpose code indicating capital/investment. The remitting bank should attach source-of-funds documentation, including audited accounts, dividend resolution, or loan agreement, and the Luxembourg bank will perform a sanctions and MLRO check. For share capital in excess of the minimum, a Luxembourg notary certifies the notarized deed and bank certificate; the RCS filing follows. No Central Bank approval or exchange control license is required; only the standard CSSF/AML compliance gates and a debt-to-equity compatibility test apply where a shareholder loan is used.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct T/T settlement to suppliers/distributors; (ii) commercial letters of credit issued under ICC UCP 600 via SWIFT MT700 to overseas beneficiary banks; (iii) SEPA Credit Transfer/Instant payment instructions for intra-European EUR payments; and (iv) TARGET2 gross settlement for high-value euro payments. Documentary trade payments require compliant commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading/CMRs, certificates of origin and, where applicable, phytosanitary/food-safety certificates. The SARL's account mandate must clearly evidence dual signatory authorization for all outbound flows above the agreed threshold, with recurring counterparty screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX spot and forward contracts with CSSF-authorized credit institutions, principally EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, and EUR/SEK/CHF tenors aligned to the cash-flow cycle, under an ISDA/CSA or local master agreement with collateral posting.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts for illiquid emerging-market currencies, concluded only with a regulated Luxembourg bank or EEA investment firm and backed by a full netting and credit-support annex.

FX swaps and cross-currency swaps for working-capital or capital-injection conversion, entered under a negotiated ISDA 2002 master agreement, with valuation, breakage clauses, and internal treasury delegation.

Foreign exchange options and zero-cost collars for manufacturing-input or export-revenue currencies, structured only as hedging instruments and not speculative, with board-approved VaR/notional limits and trade confirmation under EMIR clearing obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary general meeting of shareholders (annual general meeting) and written minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book maintained at registered office; not filed with an authority unless amending bylaws
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each financial year; e.g., 30 June for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors/managers may incur civil liability; shareholders may request the court to appoint a person to convene the meeting; persistent failure is considered in administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes) and filing with Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after adoption and no later than eight months after the financial year-end; e.g., 31 August for 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice and administrative fines; directors may be held jointly liable for damage to creditors; repeated non-filing for three consecutive years may result in involuntary strike-off (radiation) and compulsory liquidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership (UBO register declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) administered by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 15 September; any change (including shareholding transfer) must be filed within 30 days of the relevant event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of up to EUR 10,000; criminal penalties for intentional omission or false statements; failure to file may additionally result in reporting to anti-money-laundering authorities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax return package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year companies, electronic filing by 31 December of the following tax year; an extension may be requested through a registered tax professional
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; late-filing penalties up to 10% of assessed tax (capped in normal cases); directors' co-liability may be asserted in recovery proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a réviseur d'entreprises (approved statutory auditor) when, for two consecutive financial years, the company exceeds at least two of: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average of 50 employees in the year. Audit is also compulsory for public companies, credit institutions, insurance undertakings, and if ordered by shareholders holding at least one-tenth of subscribed capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU as transposed by the Law of 19 December 2002, subsequently amended); IFRS as adopted by the EU is available for consolidated accounts and may be used in certain permitted cases.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: All registered undertakings must confirm through the RBE electronic portal, by 15 September each year, that the registered beneficial-owner information is accurate and up to date. Any transfer of shares changing control or identity of beneficial owners must additionally be notified by the obliged entity within 30 days; the annual confirmation does not replace this transactional updating obligation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate effective headline rate for commercial companies in Luxembourg City (FY 2024/2025), composed of: (i) resident corporate income tax (CIT) of 17.00% on taxable profits exceeding EUR 175,000 (15.00% on the first EUR 175,000 bracket); (ii) unemployment fund surcharge of 7.00% calculated on the CIT amount; (iii) municipal business tax (IFC) of 6.75% applied on taxable commercial profit after statutory abatement.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Investment tax credit of 20% on qualifying investments up to EUR 150,000 and 10% above that ceiling; R&D tax credit of 50% on qualifying research expenditure; participation exemption granting a 100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains where the SARL holds at least 10% (or an acquisition price of at least EUR 6,000,000) and maintains the holding for at least 12 months; IP Box regime exempting 80% of qualifying IP-derived income, yielding an effective rate near 4.99%; no notional interest deduction for ICCN (old SIRe regime grandfathered only).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite statutory carryforward under Luxembourg direct tax law (LIR Art. 114) with no time-bar expiry; however, annual utilization of losses is statutorily capped: losses may offset up to EUR 1,000,000 of annual taxable income without restriction plus 50% of the portion of taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000. Carryback is not permitted. Freezing the schema default of 5 years would misstate Luxembourg law; the operative rule is unlimited forward term with utilization cap.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Model 362 (Annual corporate income tax return for sociétés, covering combined CIT, unemployment surcharge, municipal business tax, and ancillary schedules); supplementary net wealth tax return filed under Model 770; mandatory electronic filing through the MyGuichet secure e-space (eSpace MonTiers for accredited agents) or the ACD direct e-filing portal for large taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the Model 362 return is statutorily due on 30 April of the following calendar year; administratively, the Luxembourg direct tax administration (ACD) customarily grants extensions to 30 September upon request filed by a registered tax advisor; subsequent ex officio assessments follow after the deadline is missed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal form (SARL), RCS Luxembourg registration number, AED tax identification number, registered office, share capital, names and addresses of managers, principal commercial activity (NACE 1079).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident SARL with a Luxembourg permanent establishment or effectively managed undertaking files under the same Model 362 using the AED number; appoint an authorized resident representative (EIR) and provide the foreign tax identification number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable commercial profit before offsets: net turnover from instant rice noodle manufacturing, less deductible operating expenses, inventory movements, depreciation, and provisions, adjusted for hidden reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Luxembourg-source industrial and commercial profit from the PE; attach the statutory annual accounts (balance sheet and profit/loss account) per Luxembourg GAAP and a reconciliation between accounting profit and taxable profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenditure (fictitious directors fees, excessive interest, member's salaries where no genuine activity, 50% of non-vouchered entertainment costs) and claims of tax exemptions (participation exemption schedule, IP Box 80% deduction).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident must restrict IP Box claims to qualifying IP actually developed or acquired with Luxembourg substance and not subsidized by state aids; file the annex with full title, cost ledger, and nexus ratio.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carryforward schedule of prior-year tax losses applied against current taxable income, applying the EUR 1,000,000 unrestricted offset plus 50% of the surplus limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses economically connected to the Luxembourg PE or Luxembourg-source activities are eligible; foreign branch losses are excluded and cannot be carried into the Luxembourg computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax abatement applied to the IFC base: horizontal deduction applicable to all companies carrying on a commercial activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The abatement is available on the Luxembourg PE's taxable commercial profit; no additional schedule required for non-residents beyond the standard Cadre E computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of investment tax credit and R&D tax credit: 20% of qualifying acquisitions not exceeding EUR 150,000 plus 10% above, and 50% of eligible R&D labor and depreciation expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-resident entity carrying on manufacture through a Luxembourg PE may take the credit only for qualifying assets allocated to that PE and included in the Luxembourg tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax computation: taxable profit allocated between IFC base and CIT base; CIT at 15%/17% progressive bands, unemployment surcharge at 7% of CIT, IFC at the communal coefficient (6.75% standard in Luxembourg City); summary of instalments and balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No withholding is made through this return; treaty exemptions or non-discrimination claims are documented in an annex and do not reduce the headline rates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic penalty of 10% of the assessed CIT and IFC, increased to 25% after the expiry of a further 30-day grace period; the ACD may impose ex officio taxation (taxation d'office) based on estimate, invalidating the taxpayer's favorable evidence; late-payment interest accrues monthly at 0.6% (7.2% per annum); administrative fines range from EUR 250 to EUR 25,000 and, in aggravated cases, criminal fines up to EUR 250,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends distributed by an SARL to non-resident shareholders. The rate is reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the beneficial owner is an EU/EEA company holding at least 10% of the SARL's capital for an uninterrupted 12-month period; under comprehensive DTA treaties the rate is typically 5% for substantial holdings (e.g. 10% under LU-US; 10% under LU-CN unless the Chinese corporate holder owns 25% and meeting treaty tests, then 5%); domestic and treaty relief require proof of beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: (i) Obtain the official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the shareholder's residence state and, where applicable, a Beneficial Ownership Declaration; (ii) deliver the original or duly certified TRC and declaration to the Luxembourg paying SARL before the dividend resolution is executed so that the reduced rate is applied at source; (iii) for EU parent relief, complete and submit Form 166 (attestation de résidence) and the eligibility worksheet evidencing the 10% or more holding and the 12-month holding period, with ACD pre-authorization via the e-space portal where required; (iv) if the appropriate treaty rate was not applied at source, the non-resident shareholder files a refund claim with the ACD using the standard reimbursement application (form 260/270) within the statutory limitation period of five years; (v) the Luxembourg SARL must retain copies of TRCs and declarations for at least ten years to defend against retroactive WHT reassessment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on cross-border royalty and interest payments in Luxembourg is 0% under domestic law, as Luxembourg does not enact scheduler WHT on such outbound payments; DTA rates are correspondingly 0% under most treaties including LU-US (Art. 11-12) and LU-CN; however, the payments must be economically genuine: royalty attribution must be supported by IP title held by the Luxembourg entity and substance, and interest deduction requires arm's length pricing under LIR Art. 56 and the ATAD interest limitation rule (30% EBITDA cap, EUR 3,000,000 de minimis threshold).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Luxembourg Local File and Master File documentation apply where the SARL belongs to a multinational group with consolidated net turnover of at least EUR 50,000,000, or where the aggregate value of controlled transactions in the fiscal year exceeds EUR 100,000; documentation must be furnished to the ACD within 15 days of a formal demand (Law of 24 February 2023 codifying LIR Art. 56 and ACD Transfer Pricing Circular 164/2023).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations statute, but substance requirements flow from (i) LIR Art. 6, requiring the effective place of management to be situated in Luxembourg; (ii) LIR Art. 56, requiring arm's length remuneration for all functions, assets, and risks; (iii) OECD BEPS and EU ATAD anti-abuse rules, including the GAAR and the controlled foreign company rules; a rice-noodle manufacturing SARL with physical production lines, quality-control laboratories, raw-material inventory, local payroll, and managerial decision-making in Luxembourg fully satisfies the substance doctrine, whereas a letterbox entity routing 100% margins without local activity will be recharacterised or disregarded; the ACD will pierce the arrangement and reassess at the full 24.94% with penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating fictitious purchase invoices for rice, vegetable oil, or packaging materials from non-existent suppliers in third countries, fabricating inventory counts, or diverting cash sales of instant noodles off-ledger; intentional concealment of taxable commercial profit from the ACD.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion under LIR Art. 395 and the General Tax Procedure Act: fines from EUR 10,000 to EUR 250,000, imprisonment up to 5 years; civil reassessment with a 25% penalty surcharge and denial of all deductions linked to the falsified documentation; publication of the sanction by the tax administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant or managing director who signed false vouchers or knowingly allowed off-book revenue is personally liable for the full additional tax, interest, and penalties; the corporate veil is pierced where the SARL is unable to pay, and courts have ordered direct civil restitution from the director's personal estate, issued exit travel bans, and imposed custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting the actual rice-noodle production in a foreign affiliate while the Luxembourg SARL issues high-margin invoices without employees, production premises, warehouse assets, or genuine operational control; using the SARL as a bare invoicing conduit to siphon profits into Luxembourg at artificial margins.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation or disregard of the SARL's legal form under the OECD CAAR and ATAD GAAR; reassessment of the full 24.94% CIT on the deemed Luxembourg profit; denial of DTA and EU directive benefits; retroactive interest and penalties of up to 25%; potential mutual agreement and secondary adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Sole or shadow directors are jointly liable for the SARL's liabilities under para. 435 of the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies where inadequate capitalisation or artificial restructuring caused damage; sanctions include disqualification from holding directorships for up to 10 years, personal assessment for the unpaid CIT, and criminal fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Cash Transactions and Suspicious Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting repeated cash payments above EUR 10,000 for cartons of instant noodles from unverified importers without performing customer due diligence or beneficial-ownership verification; deliberately failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports with the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) despite red flags of structured payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004, as amended by the Parity Law of 10 July 2020: administrative fines up to EUR 1,000,000 imposed by the Ministry of Justice/Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier; freezing of the funds involved; publication of the sanction and suspension or revocation of the food-manufacturing licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who consciously or negligently omitted the CTR/SAR filing are criminally liable with imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 500,000; in bankruptcy, the directors are civilly liable to creditors and the tax authority where the AML failure is the proximate cause of the SARL's insolvency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Persistent Late Filing, Non-Payment, and Clandestine Manufacturing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Model 362 for three consecutive fiscal years, complete non-payment of provisional CIT instalments, operation of production before obtaining the required food-safety license, and use of undeclared subcontracted lines in the Luosifen supply chain; obstruction of ACD audits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ex officio assessment on the ACD's unfavourable estimate; late-filing penalties escalating to 25%; late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; reassessment within a ten-year limitation period where a taxpayer acted with intent to conceal; dissolution action initiated by the ACD; revocation of the RCS registration for solvent companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors are personally liable for the increased tax burden arising from gross negligence (faute lourde) or bad faith under general Luxembourg civil law; travel bans and exit restrictions have been imposed in aggravated cases, and the directors may be sentenced to imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years, with a prohibition on managing any commercial company for up to 10 years.
